approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted scored observations. It retains a bounded score-ranked breeding population, samples parents from favored score bands, and generates a fresh surplus pool through connected-fragment crossover and local mutation walks. Its crossover normally cuts one non-ring single bond in each parent and joins the retained fragments with one bond; where no such cut exists, it can attach a whole molecule at an available hydrogen site. Optional finishing mutation follows crossover. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identity checks reject invalid or duplicate proposals. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated sampled score functions choose which fresh pool members receive evaluation. Accepted feedback updates both the model archive and the greedy breeding population.
approach.novelty: Add one two-cut ring-segment construction option to the existing crossover. When both actual scored parents have an eligible isolated nonaromatic ring, give the original crossover and the new option equal probability. The new option takes a connected ring segment, with all its attached subgraphs, from each parent and reconnects their two open ends into a ring. This supplies direct access to alternative two-attachment ring connectivities while keeping the original route available. Earlier siblings changed donor compatibility or excluded parent copies, and an older experiment protected every first-parent ring; those exposed changes lost score. This experiment changes which ring products can be constructed, without imposing those restrictions or assuming that distinct strings or preserved rings are useful. Its value depends on the new products surviving ordinary checks, receiving evaluations and improving the complete search.

observed_bottleneck: The code Parent n-62daf219c70a has no two-attachment ring-segment crossover interface: GraphOperators.fragment selects only non-ring SINGLE cuts or the inherited whole-fragment hydrogen-attachment fallback, and crossover adds one interfragment SINGLE bond. It therefore cannot directly exchange two-ended ring paths in one crossover, although separate ordinary mutations can form, open or alter rings. The actual three Parent summary.json and run.log files are present and complete, with macro mean 0.5956696497334577, population SD 0.02659287062806747, and seed macros 0.625411930168826, 0.560865654270234 and 0.600731364761313. Its published molecular report describes limited leading-family alternatives alongside useful conventional cyclic amines and persistent difficult ring geometry; this motivates a construction-access hypothesis, not a claim that low ring counts or diversity caused endpoint loss. A read-only pre-registration audit, using the descriptor law below on recorded actual Parent pairs and excluding duplicate emitted receipts, finds 34334 crossover attempts, 11111 eligible first-parent sources, 11263 eligible second-parent sources and 9293 jointly eligible pairs across 2330 examined parent identities. Opportunity is highly uneven: the three deco_hop cells have 0, 1 and 0 jointly eligible pairs; these are observations for analysis, never candidate task branches. No ring product was constructed or scored in that audit, and inherited outcomes on those pairs do not label hypothetical recombinants. Current isolated removal n-767d2ce08797 loses 0.054937284705486644 with all three seed macros lower, supporting retention of ordinary crossover but not this extension. Current compatible-donor n-eb61315a5619 exposes 354 nonidentical evaluated descendants yet loses 0.020270634588430703; current parent-copy exclusion n-bddb1dbe8e32 exposes 356 conditioned nonidentical evaluations yet loses 0.10265273096567833. Older full-ring retention n-822f049d9c70 achieves physical core preservation and substantial evaluation exposure but loses 0.015306780861481665 against its different Parent n-fc2c108a5253. Those contrary results remain boundaries on useful-recombination and ring-preservation claims, not current matched evidence for a two-cut construction.
hypothesis: Extend the inherited two-parent crossover with an equally weighted two-cut ring-segment mode only when both actual scored parents have eligible isolated nonaromatic-ring descriptors, joining one complete retained component from each parent by two single bonds while preserving the ordinary single-cut route and its no-support random law.

finding_summary.headline: Ring recombination reached evaluation and later breeding, but every seed mean fell
finding_summary.insights:
Failed construction and a globally blocked evaluation route do not explain this result: the new two-attachment products were built correctly, evaluated and reused. The complete exposed loss therefore supports a negative total contribution from this particular extension under the tested search composition, while leaving the separate evidence for ordinary crossover intact. Greater local win frequency is misleading here because the generating-parent references also became weaker. One positive endpoint even occurred in a run that never selected ring mode; its eligible mode draw changed the subsequent random stream, so that gain cannot be assigned to a new ring product.

The chemistry narrows the remaining limitation. The search now reaches medium and large nitrogen/carbonyl rings, including 72 accepted proposals with rings of at least twelve atoms, yet access to those graphs does not establish useful arrangements or feasible geometry. Finishing mutation also matters: the new typed ring pattern survives in all 124 pure evaluated recombinants but only 43 of the 55 finished ones. Aromatic, amine and carbonyl families remain well represented, alongside reactive bonds, difficult sulfur and small-ring structures, and unspecified stereochemistry. More scaffold identities and fewer molecules in a limited bond-alert screen coexist with lower scores. The unresolved question is which altered ancestors, pool competition and accepted feedback paths produced the endpoint loss; the observed cohorts do not supply scores for unselected alternatives or isolate an individual ring segment’s causal value. This complete failure closes the registered test without a ring-size, mode-weight or donor-preference sweep.
finding_summary.results:
Ring mode was selected on 5,498 of 10,982 jointly eligible opportunities. All 5,496 products constructed below the atom limit conserved the selected source components and made the intended two attachments; two selected choices exceeded the inherited atom limit before construction. There were 4,957 immediate products distinct from both parents and 539 parent copies. The route delivered 179 evaluated descendants of nonidentical constructions: 124 pure crossovers and 55 with finishing mutation. Another 11 evaluations gained novelty only by mutating a parent copy. All 174 nonidentical descendants with a later opportunity entered the next model fit, 96 later bred, 35 beat their best generating parent and 15 improved the incumbent. Exposure was uneven: none of the six zaleplon and decoration-hop runs evaluated a ring-mode descendant.

All fifteen Child task runs completed. Mean final Top-1 score fell from 0.595670 to 0.550623, a paired change of -0.045046 against the required +0.002. Seed macro changes were -0.014404, -0.020055 and -0.100680; ten task-seed endpoints declined, two improved and three were unchanged. Seed population SD increased from 0.026593 to 0.045826. The largest losses were docking seed 2 (-0.309828) and sitagliptin seeds 0 and 2 (-0.113615 and -0.189390). Across the entire search, local parent beats nevertheless rose from 629 to 652 and incumbent increases from 258 to 266.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic output includes cyclic amines and macrocyclic dicarbonyls, but also reactive bonds and doubtful ring geometry
molecular.overall_character:
Assessed n-870ed6964d46 against published code Parent n-62daf219c70a using every supplied actual Search trajectory: all five tasks, seeds 0, 1 and 2, and all 30 Child/Parent files. All paths exist; each file has 300 consecutive finite-score observations, comprising 10 initial molecules and 290 accepted optimizer proposals. The complete Child molecular digest is exactly reproduced from those files, including every excerpt, score span, unique count and string counter; all task summary endpoints and paired differences reconcile. Both context.comparison.child_complete and paired_complete are true, with no profile-mismatched seed or missing comparison. The fixed initial molecules and scores agree in every pairing. The complete molecular identity/score trajectories are identical for zaleplon_mpo seed 2 and deco_hop seeds 0 and 2. Those null cells are retained explicitly. Digest final_molecules are the last pooled proposals from seed 2, not per-seed incumbents; score_span includes initial observations, whereas best_molecules and worst_molecules describe optimizer proposals. All quantities below use actual accepted molecules and existing scores; no unselected pool alternative is scored or characterized as if evaluated.

The Child makes substituted indole amides, imides and vicinal diketones; dense linked nitrogen heterocycles; flexible and cyclic aryl amines; sulfur-rich cages; nitrogen/carbonyl macrocycles; and fluorinated, partially unsaturated ring systems. Its 4,350 accepted proposals have 1–120 heavy atoms, median 28; 4,244 contain a perceived ring and 4,177 an aromatic atom. The digest's taskwise ring-closure-string incidence is 0.9655–0.9851 and aromatic-string incidence 0.9184–0.9770; these are molecule-level text incidences, not aromatic-atom fractions. RDKit detects nonaromatic rings in 2,971 proposals, compared with 2,757 in Parent, and saturated rings in 1,610 versus 1,266. Rich ring chemistry therefore coexists with much narrower leading families within individual seeds. There are 1,977/1,851 distinct Child/Parent typed Murcko cores, 1,172/1,118 generic Murcko cores and 655/631 generic ring-only graphs across the whole panel. Per-task and per-seed changes are mixed. Seventy-two Child proposals have a perceived ring of at least 12 atoms, all within the nitrogen/carbonyl macrocycle stream; this count is 9, 1 and 62 by seed, versus zero in each matching Parent cell. The largest Child perceived ring has 23 atoms. These counts establish access to varied graphs, not useful topology, geometric feasibility or synthesis.

Local chemical liabilities remain substantial but are not universal: 634 Child proposals have an N–halogen bond, 123 O–halogen, 294 O–O and 12 halogen–halogen; 1,010 have at least one of these motifs, versus 1,490 in Parent. Those overlapping motif counts form a limited structural screen, not a complete reactivity or safety model. Several near-leading flexible or piperidine-containing amines have none of these bonds; conversely, an alert-free sulfur cage and small unsaturated ring graphs remain chemically questionable. RDKit flags potential tetrahedral centres in 2,534 Child proposals versus 2,408 Parent proposals, yet all are unassigned, and there are no explicitly assigned atom chiral tags or double-bond stereo tags in either accepted stream. All atoms also have zero formal charge. Neutral aliphatic amines are visibly present, so this does not mean an absence of basic centres or establish a physical protonation state. Synthetic plausibility is a cautious structural reading: recognizable amides, aryl groups, piperidines, sulfoxides and macrocyclic motifs coexist with N–halogen/O–halogen chemistry, peroxides, complex bridges and small-ring unsaturation. No conformer, stability measurement or synthetic route was supplied, and graph sanitation is not such evidence.

Audit definitions: RDKit 2023.09.6 parsed all 9,000 trajectory rows. Reported rings are its perceived atom rings. Typed cores use GetScaffoldForMol; generic cores use MakeScaffoldGeneric on that scaffold; both omit stereochemistry and map every empty scaffold to one <acyclic> sentinel. The separate generic ring-only graph retains only perceived ring bonds and their incident atoms, removes exocyclic atoms and inter-ring linkers, then makes atoms carbon and bonds single, preserving disconnected-ring multiplicity. Ten highest-scoring proposals per cell are ordered by the existing score and then evaluation number; this is a descriptive chemistry stratum. The aliphatic-amine proxy requires neutral, nonaromatic trivalent N with single bonds to carbon only, excluding aromatic carbon neighbors and carbons double-bonded to N/O/S; it is not a measured basicity or protonation rule. Ring labels, exact core identity and substructure similarity are structural observations. Pedigree ancestry requires its own accepted-parent receipts; literal retained source atoms require source-indexed maps at construction and separate post-edit mapping. These trajectories carry neither, and this report makes no ancestry, atom-conservation or component-contribution inference from scaffold coverage. Reproducible full-panel measurements and file hashes are in .slots/L01-resume-20260928/r22-slot0-molecular/audit.json. Inherited chemical gaps retain their first-recorded n-c55c3d520a2c origin and original profile boundary, their published n-62daf219c70a recurrence, and the present current-profile recurrence; no historical effect estimates are pooled.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 accepted proposals span 1–38 heavy atoms, median 24; 840 contain perceived rings and 838 contain aromatic atoms. Seed 0's 25-heavy-atom leader at evaluation 196 is an ethyl/methyl/methoxy-substituted indole carboxamide linked to chloropyridine, with fluorine bonded directly to the indole nitrogen. Seed 1's 25-heavy-atom leader at evaluation 275 has an N-aminomethyl indole joined through an acyclic imide to fluoropyridine; it contains carbon-bound halogen and no N–halogen bond. Seed 2's 24-heavy-atom leader at evaluation 294 keeps an N-chloroindole–aryl vicinal diketone with an aminomethyl substituent. All three leaders have three perceived rings, with sizes 5, 6 and 6. These retain compact fused aromatic/carbonyl organization rather than lacking rings. N–halogen-containing proposals are 132, 14 and 25 by seed, compared with 190, 230 and 25 in Parent. Seed 2 is molecularly identical to Parent; seeds 0 and 1 change family details in different directions. Top-ten generic-core counts are 2, 4 and 2, compared with Parent 3, 1 and 2, so neither total collapse nor uniform diversification is supported. Across all 870 accepted proposals, Child/Parent distinct typed Murcko cores are 256/295, generic Murcko cores 107/124, and generic ring-only graphs 57/70. These are different structural coverage measurements under the fixed acyclic convention, not independent chemical families or atom-provenance counts.
liabilities: N–F, N–Cl and N–Br substitutions on an indole nitrogen are not interchangeable with ordinary aryl carbon–halogen bonds; their local reactivity requires assessment.
Vicinal diketones, acyclic imides and N-aminomethyl substitution introduce context-dependent reactivity or stability questions; recognized group names are not a synthetic route.
Tiny late fragments lose the composite framework, while additional polar branches can also lower score. Neither liability supports a universal size or heteroatom rule.
missing_features: The favorable aromatic/carbonyl organization is demonstrated, but a consistently conventional local nitrogen environment at the same leading score is not; the high-scoring N–C imide and N–H diketone are real counterexamples to any claim that ordinary nitrogen substitution is inaccessible.

Independent, chemically credible alternatives to indole-centered leading families remain incompletely demonstrated. Generic-core and ring-graph variation measures cannot establish that the alternatives have suitable geometry or synthesis.
The trajectory does not reveal an exact missing pharmacophore, and it does not support simply adding rings, nitrogen or fluorine.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide (seed 0, evaluation 9) scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-0 N-fluoro/pyridyl-amide leader reaches 0.4387992465191, and seed 1's imide with ordinary N–C substitution reaches 0.4279555137322127. Seed 2's diketone reaches 0.438972502037081, while its N–H indole/azaaryl diketone at evaluation 220 reaches 0.4259670894318899 without N–halogen. Thus the observed reward accompanies a combined aromatic and carbonyl arrangement, not a demonstrated requirement for a reactive nitrogen substituent. A more elaborated seed-2 relative at evaluation 297 scores 0.2537139094300773; extra aminoalkyl substitution is not uniformly rewarded. Removing most of the framework leaves seed 0's final pyridyl acetamide at 6.9339977595548645e-09, and acetylene at evaluation 279 scores 0.0. The ten lowest-scoring proposals in seeds 0 and 1 are all acyclic small graphs. These contrasts do not identify an exact absent target motif. Existing Child/Parent final Top-1 values are seed 0: 0.4387992465/0.3940514207 (difference +0.0447478258); seed 1: 0.4279555137/0.4741170181 (difference -0.0461615044); seed 2: 0.4389725020/0.4389725020 (difference +0.0000000000). These are descriptive paired outcomes, not scores assigned by this report.

per_task.generated_character: Accepted proposals span 1–100 heavy atoms, median 33; 850/870 contain rings and 849 aromatic atoms. Seed 0's 30-heavy-atom leader at evaluation 281 has five perceived rings: a quinazoline-like aromatic region joined to a densely fused/bridged nitrogen/carbonyl/thione region, with aryl chlorine, O–F and a fluorinated chloromethyl-ether appendage. Seed 1's 38-heavy-atom leader at evaluation 287 has six perceived rings, a linked aza/oxygen heterocycle-carbonyl assembly, a carbon-bound aryl fluoride, a chlorinated alkynyl side chain and an O–O-containing ring region. liabilities: O–F on an aromatic oxygen, a halomethyl ether, thione, and crowded ring junctions make the seed-0 graph a questionable synthetic target despite its recognizable heterocyclic portions.

O–O bonds occur in 251/870 Child proposals, including ring and linker contexts; other leaders retain nitrite and N=S groups. These are distinct local chemistry issues, not an objection to all ethers, heterocycles or nitriles.
No synthesis, stable tautomer or conformation is demonstrated for the complex aromatic-labelled O–O ring region or the additional cross-linked products.
missing_features: Reliable access to conventional peripheral chemistry around the favorable linked heterocyclic arrangements is not demonstrated at the strongest score. The close no-peroxide seed-1 example is a useful counterexample to a universal need for the peroxide-containing region.
Geometry and stereochemical identity of the densely connected ring regions are unresolved. The lead seed-0 graph has potential tetrahedral centres but no specified stereochemistry.

The strongest compact nitrogen-rich arrangement appears in one seed while the others lead with different families; more perceived rings in the changed seed did not establish the same molecular organization.

Large, flexible, polyfunctional and halogenated proposals coexist with more recognizable piperidine/sulfoxide and flexible tertiary-amine candidates. Synthetic handles do not establish solubility, stability or selectivity.

Stereochemical identity is missing in 845/870 proposals with RDKit-detected potential tetrahedral centres. The sulfoxide and substituted cyclic-amine chemistry raises additional environment-specific stereochemical questions beyond this tetrahedral-centre counter.

Explicit protonation and conformational states are not supplied. Neutral SMILES do not establish neutral molecules in solution, and no missing task-specific amine motif can be inferred from these examples.

liabilities: The seed-0 cross-linked aromatic-labelled appendage and seed-2 four-membered diene impose serious ring-geometry questions. Fewer cumulated double bonds does not establish that these replacement graphs are feasible.
N–F occurs in the seed-1 and seed-2 leaders, while N–N and N–O environments appear in other portions of the stream. A carbon-bound fluoromethyl group is chemically distinct from an N–F bond.
A large local score change can coexist with unchanged questionable core geometry; the recorded objective provides no synthesis, stability or biological validation.
missing_features: The favorable compact fluorinated/nitrogen-carbonyl organization is present, but geometrically credible alternatives are not established at the leading scores. Ordinary cyclopropyl groups must be distinguished from a four-membered diene or an aromatic-labelled cross-linked six-carbon graph.

Tautomeric, conformational and aromatic identity of the enolic and large aromatic-labelled ring regions remains unresolved; lowercase SMILES and sanitization cannot establish a stable aromatic conformation.

Stereochemical identity is unspecified in 535/870 proposals with potential tetrahedral centres, including substituted fused and enolic ring environments. More fluorine, generic cores or perceived rings is not itself an identified missing capability.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. Child leaders reach 0.5374063569697202, 0.45202855439739353 and 0.5314955312223999 by seed, each below its paired Parent. A close seed-2 contrast adds a hydroxyl to the leader's difluoromethyl carbon: evaluation 295 scores 0.006624711698425933 while retaining the difficult ring framework. That local sensitivity supports the importance of the whole substitution/property arrangement; it does not validate the ring geometry or show that more polarity is always useful. A different seed-2 fused-dione relative at evaluation 262 reaches 0.430281699299315 with carbon-bound fluorines and no N–F; seed 0's leader also has no N–halogen. Thus N–F is not a universal high-score requirement, although these counterexamples retain other geometric liabilities. Isolated F at seed 1 evaluation 218 scores 1.1043196211273875e-26, so fluorination alone is insufficient. The strongest seed-2 Parent has a different small-ring cumulene family; that historical graph is chemically questionable too, and its larger score is not a physical plausibility benchmark. The exact absent target-specific pharmacophore cannot be recovered from this output. Existing Child/Parent final Top-1 values are seed 0: 0.5374063570/0.6510211907 (difference -0.1136148337); seed 1: 0.4520285544/0.4870057306 (difference -0.0349771762); seed 2: 0.5314955312/0.7208853668 (difference -0.1893898356). These are descriptive paired outcomes, not scores assigned by this report.

transferable_gaps.evidence: First recorded as a molecular gap in n-c55c3d520a2c under its original profile, then reproduced in published baseline n-62daf219c70a; the current measurements are a recurrence/extension in n-870ed6964d46 against that baseline on the complete current-profile Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, batch 10, 300 observations per task. Among 4,350 accepted Child proposals, 634 contain N–halogen, 123 O–halogen, 294 O–O and 12 halogen–halogen bonds; their overlapping union is 1,010 versus Parent 1,490. This aggregate decrease is not uniform: one nitrogen/carbonyl stream has 89 such proposals versus Parent 22. Some leaders have ordinary carbon-bound halogens and tertiary/cyclic amines without these bonds. An alert-free sulfur cage also shows that this limited motif list is not a complete chemical-quality test.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments around otherwise useful molecular frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need bond-environment-aware alternatives that retain favorable functional context while distinguishing carbon-bound halogens, amines and ordinary ethers from reactive heteroatom attachments and unusual valence environments. Use accepted task-local feedback to evaluate alternatives. These associations neither prove a universal filter improves score nor attribute the bonds to a particular crossover or mutation component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: First recorded as a molecular gap in n-c55c3d520a2c under its original profile, then reproduced in published baseline n-62daf219c70a; the current measurements are a recurrence/extension in n-870ed6964d46 against that baseline on the complete current-profile Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, batch 10, 300 observations per task. The Child has 655 generic ring-only graphs versus Parent 631 and 72 accepted molecules with a perceived ring of at least 12 atoms versus Parent 1 across the whole panel. The 72 occur in one stream, with 9, 1 and 62 by seed, while the matching Parent cells each have zero. Other leaders contain a cross-linked aromatic-labelled six-carbon graph, a four-membered diene and a hydrogen-bearing hypervalent sulfur cage. Recognizable piperidine/cyclopropyl/sulfoxide and flexible aryl-amine examples also score highly. More ring coverage and ordinary small rings must therefore be distinguished from these specific feasibility concerns.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output demonstrates ring construction without consistently demonstrating geometrically credible unsaturation, bridge connectivity or macrocyclic context.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations would need to account for bond geometry, ring size, bridge connectivity and local functional context, offering alternatives whose usefulness can be tested without presuming that extra ring graphs help. Macrocycles and small saturated rings are not categorically implausible. This is an output capability gap, not an activation verdict or a causal diagnosis of the new construction mode. Ring labels, Murcko coverage, pedigree ancestry and literal retained source atoms require separate evidence.

transferable_gaps.evidence: First recorded as a molecular gap in n-c55c3d520a2c under its original profile, then reproduced in published baseline n-62daf219c70a; the current measurements are a recurrence/extension in n-870ed6964d46 against that baseline on the complete current-profile Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, batch 10, 300 observations per task. RDKit finds potential tetrahedral centres in 2,534/4,350 Child proposals versus 2,408/4,350 Parent proposals, with all those centres unassigned. Neither stream has assigned atom chiral tags or double-bond stereochemistry. Many corresponding graphs have recognizable substituted cyclic amines or polycyclic centres, rather than being uniformly achiral. Formal charges are also absent, but neutral aliphatic amines are common; this is a different representation issue.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not specify stereochemical identity when its output creates potentially stereogenic saturated or bridged environments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representation and transformations would need to preserve or resolve stereochemical identity where appropriate, distinguishing stable stereocentres from achiral or configurationally unstable environments. Treat protonation and tautomerism separately. Unspecified identity is directly observed; a score penalty or a benefit from any stereo-resolution policy has not been measured here.

transferable_gaps.evidence: First recorded as a molecular gap in n-c55c3d520a2c under its original profile, then reproduced in published baseline n-62daf219c70a; the current measurements are a recurrence/extension in n-870ed6964d46 against that baseline on the complete current-profile Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, batch 10, 300 observations per task. There are 112 Child proposals with at most five heavy atoms versus 123 Parent proposals, including late small graphs at their observed score floors. At the opposite extreme the Child reaches 120 heavy atoms; one leading sulfur-containing family comes from a stream averaging 45.51 heavy atoms versus Parent 31.52. A more cross-linked heterocycle has a lower score than its compact leader, while conventional smaller aryl-amine examples retain nearby high scores. The favorable direction is conditional on molecular context.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator still loses useful functional context in tiny fragments while also emitting excessive or difficult elaborations of promising families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-local evidence could guide context-preserving fragmentation, simplification and recombination, with enough functional arrangement retained to make the proposal informative. Neither a fixed minimum size nor automatic growth follows from the observations. Candidate distinctness and sanitation alone cannot distinguish a useful simplification from loss of the entire learned arrangement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: First recorded as a molecular gap in n-c55c3d520a2c under its original profile, then reproduced in published baseline n-62daf219c70a; the current measurements are a recurrence/extension in n-870ed6964d46 against that baseline on the complete current-profile Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, batch 10, 300 observations per task. Whole-panel Child/Parent counts are 1,977/1,851 typed Murcko cores, 1,172/1,118 generic Murcko cores and 655/631 generic ring-only graphs under the same single acyclic-sentinel convention. Within one changed stream, generic-core counts rise from 87 to 148 in one seed while the supplied endpoint is lower; elsewhere they fall from 406 to 354 across the three seeds despite access to large rings. Three complete paired molecular trajectories are unchanged. Leading subsets still consist mainly of close aromatic, nitrogen/carbonyl or aryl-amine variants, with useful conventional counterexamples and structurally different seed families.
transferable_gaps.gap: Independent plausible alternatives to the leading chemistry remain uneven even when many distinct core and ring graphs are observed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need chemically credible scaffold alternatives that preserve the functional relationships supported by its own accepted observations. Assess structural coverage, subsequent evaluated usefulness and chemical feasibility separately; no core-count target, founder label or source-atom claim substitutes for the others. The evidence does not show that maximizing diversity improves score or identify an individual component's contribution.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
